2610.08401.title: GeoPID: Decomposing and Steering Visual Information in Vision-Language Models
2610.08401.paper_summary: While recent vision-language models (VLMs) have shown outstanding performance across diverse applications, they tend to under-use visual information and over-rely on textual context. In this work, we propose \textsc{GeoPID}, a training-free framework that analyzes multimodal information within VLMs from a geometric perspective. \textsc{GeoPID} decomposes information into Redundant, Modality-Unique, and Synergistic components through the geometric relationships between visual and textual representation subspaces. Through an extensive analysis across 22 VLMs and 14 benchmarks, we confirm that correct predictions exhibit stronger vision-unique components when questions strongly require visual grounding. Building on this geometric analysis, we introduce a targeted intervention technique that selectively amplifies visual representations along the vision-unique subspace during inference. As a result, visual grounding capabilities were enhanced without any additional model parameter updates, achieving an average relative accuracy gain of 7.63\%.
2610.08401.paper_summary_zh: 最近的視覺-語言模型（VLMs）在多樣的應用中展現了卓越的性能，但它們往往對視覺信息的利用不足，並過度依賴文本上下文。在這項工作中，我們提出了\textsc{GeoPID}，這是一個無需訓練的框架，從幾何的角度分析VLM中的多模態信息。\textsc{GeoPID}通過視覺和文本表示子空間之間的幾何關係，將信息分解為冗餘、模態獨特和協同組件。通過對22個VLM和14個基準的廣泛分析，我們確認當問題強烈要求視覺基礎時，正確的預測展現出更強的視覺獨特組件。在這一幾何分析的基礎上，我們引入了一種針對性的干預技術，在推理過程中選擇性地放大視覺表示，沿著視覺獨特子空間進行操作。因此，視覺基礎能力得到了增強，而無需任何額外的模型參數更新，實現了平均相對準確率提升7.63%。
